meta.title: Code Heros — the programmers who build a hundred applications

hero.name: Code Heros
hero.tagline: The programmers who build a hundred applications.
hero.lede: Code Heros is a public list of programmers who have built a hundred applications, every one of them released with its source open for anyone to read. The bar to join is ten. Ten public, open-source applications put a name on the list; the count beside it runs to a hundred. Anyone can check an entry, and anyone can add one with a pull request.

items.name: Ten to join, a hundred to reach
items.body: Ten applications put a name on the list. The hundred squares beside it fill in one at a time.

items.name: Public
items.body: Every application can be opened, installed or run by anyone: a site at an address, a package on a registry, a release that downloads, an extension on a marketplace, an app in a store.

items.name: Open source
items.body: Every application's source is in a public repository that anyone can read, clone and build.

items.name: Code, and enough of it
items.body: It does not have to be an application. A library, a framework, a tool, a bot all count, on three conditions: it is code, there is enough of it to be a real piece of work, and anyone can check that it works, by opening it, installing it, or building and running it. A snippet, a template, a page of configuration or a fork of someone else's work does not count.

items.name: Checkable
items.body: An entry is one file in this repository: a name, a few links, and the list of applications. Anyone can check it against the repositories it points at, and anyone can correct it with a pull request.

heroes.title: Application heroes
heroes.none: There is no hero of 100 applications yet!

leads.title: Other programmers working to become heroes

join.title: Add yourself
join.lede: The list lives in a GitHub repository, and an entry is one pull request.

steps.name: One file
steps.body: Add data/leads/<handle>.json: your name, your links, and at least ten applications, each with its public repository.

steps.name: Pull request
steps.body: Open a pull request. A check runs on it: the file parses, there are ten applications, every repository answers. The rest is read by a person.

join.language: The list is written in English. Where a description carries a translation, the page shows it in the reader's language.
join.collected: Not every entry is written by the person it names. The people who keep the site also collect entries themselves, and those are checked and corrected the same way as any other.
join.prompt: Or copy the prompt, give it to an AI assistant with a GitHub profile, and it writes the file.
